newsitem.title: GERMANY: GRUNDIG AS FINANCE DIRECTOR RESIGNS.
newsitem.headline: GRUNDIG AS FINANCE DIRECTOR RESIGNS.

text.p: Crisis-hit German consumer electronics producer Grundig AG said on Monday that finance director Karl Heinz Wieland was leaving the board at his own request.
Wieland's resignation comes after Philips NV of the Netherlands last week decided to abandon its controlling role in Grundig and become a passive minority shareholder.
Lossmaking Grundig's supervisory board will decide on the future of the company's management next week.
Trade union leaders at the company rejected a Grundig spokesman's version that Wieland had resigned, alleging he had been sacked.
Works council leader Dieter Appelt of the IG Metall union accused the Grundig board of running down the company and said workers had lost confidence in chairman Pieter van der Wal.

Philips wanted Grundig "out of the market", Appelt told Germany's ZDF public television. He called on the Bavarian government to take over the management of Grundig until it can be stabilised, but premier Edmund Stoiber has already refused.
Workers have begun gathering signatures to protest at Van der Wal's call for the workforce to be cut to 6,000 by the turn of the century from 8,500 now.
Van der Wal said last week that Grundig would only return to profit in 1998 after three consecutive years of losses.
